chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Were the taps in the clip really his?
summary: Nierenberg notes taps out of sync in the editing, but Bubbles insists they were recorded live and nothing was cut.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: And those taps that we hear are actually your real taps?
Yeah.
Were they recorded at the same time that that was filmed?
Yup, yup.
Because in editing that sequence we found that the taps were often out of sync with the movement of your feet.
Don't know how that happened.
You're sure that they didn't put anybody else's taps in there?
What?
They didn't
put anybody else's taps -- or record the taps later after you did the whole dance?
No.
Was the dance originally longer than it is now or is the same length as your original --
About the same length.
Or did they cut any out?
Not to my knowledge, they didn't cut nothing out.
In your original act with Buck, did Buck sing along with you as you did in this film.
He could sing, yeah, he could sing, too.
Because I noticed in the film clip that Buck's voice doesn't come across very strong.
Where? What clip is that?
In this film clip. Buck's voice when he's singing together with you towards the end, his voice doesn't come across very strong.
